description: Bug 2 (Option B) — Security Center group shows nothing for accounts whose cached snapshot was never written, even though the /security page shows findings for the same resource (because the page computes them live and only the twice-weekly cron persists a snapshot). The aggregator's reader fix and the 12-digit key-form fix are already committed (d082b9f05) and the key form is confirmed correct (reader and both writers all use 'security-' + 12-digit AWS id). The remaining fix: make SecurityController.getSecurityFindings persist its LIVE-SCAN result via dashboardDataService.saveSecuritySnapshot under that same key, inside the EXISTING live-scan branch only — no new scan is ever triggered. After a user opens /security once, security-<accountId> exists and the cost drawer reaches parity on the next open. Independent of FEAT-001 (different file: the controller, not the aggregator).
steps: Read /Users/admin/Desktop/xam-latest/XamOps-New/.worktrees/sec-tab-dedup-sc-fix/.agents/tasks/cost-security-alerts-tab/context.json and this file FIRST. Then read SecurityController.getSecurityFindings (the cached branch and the live-scan fallback .thenApply(findings -> ...) block) and DashboardDataService.saveSecuritySnapshot.

In SecurityController.getSecurityFindings, inside the live-scan fallback .thenApply(findings -> { ... }) block, after `merged` is computed (merged = liveFindings.mergeInto(...); merged = resolutions.reconcileAgainstFreshScan(...)) and before `return ResponseEntity.ok(merged);`, add `dashboardDataService.saveSecuritySnapshot(cacheKey, merged);` reusing the cacheKey = "security-" + accountId already declared at the top of the method. Persist the post-merge/post-reconcile list so the snapshot matches what the page renders.
Do NOT change the cached (forceRefresh=false hit) branch, do NOT add any new scan trigger, and do NOT modify ResourceSecurityAggregationService. The aggregator must remain unable to trigger a scan.

Create a focused unit test SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest at /Users/admin/Desktop/xam-latest/XamOps-New/.worktrees/sec-tab-dedup-sc-fix/xamops-service/src/test/java/com/xammer/cloud/controller/SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest.java (there is NO existing SecurityControllerTest; ResourceSecurityControllerTest is the controller pattern reference). Use MockitoExtension and mock all 9 SecurityController constructor dependencies (securityService, cloudAccountRepository, cloudListService, dashboardDataService, excelExportService, prowlerService, liveFindings/SecurityFindingProjectionService, detectorCoverage/DetectorCoverageService, resolutions/SecurityFindingResolutionService).

Positive test: call getSecurityFindings(AWS_ID, true) so the cached branch is skipped. Stub cloudAccountRepository.findByAwsAccountId(AWS_ID) -> List.of(account) with account.getId() set; cloudListService.getRegionStatusForAccount(account, true) -> CompletableFuture.completedFuture(List.of()); securityService.getComprehensiveSecurityFindings(eq(account), anyList(), eq(true)) -> CompletableFuture.completedFuture(a small findings list); liveFindings.mergeInto(anyList(), any()) -> pass-through; resolutions.reconcileAgainstFreshScan(anyList(), any()) -> pass-through. Call .join() on the returned future, then verify(dashboardDataService).saveSecuritySnapshot(eq("security-"+AWS_ID), any()).

Negative test: call getSecurityFindings(AWS_ID, false) with a present, young cached snapshot (stub dashboardDataService.getSecuritySnapshot(eq("security-"+AWS_ID), any(), anyInt()) -> a findings list; mergeInto/filterResolved pass-through) and verify(dashboardDataService, never()).saveSecuritySnapshot(anyString(), any()) — the cached hit must not persist.

Compile and run the new test; keep ResourceSecurityControllerTest and CurInsightsControllerTest green. Stage and commit locally on branch fix/sec-tab-dedup-and-security-center with git -C /Users/admin/Desktop/xam-latest/XamOps-New/.worktrees/sec-tab-dedup-sc-fix (commit the controller + new test file; never push). Set this FEAT's status to completed and record anything the convergence step needs in findings.
acceptance_criteria: SecurityController.getSecurityFindings, on the live-scan path (forceRefresh=true or cache miss), calls dashboardDataService.saveSecuritySnapshot with key 'security-' + accountId and the merged/reconciled findings list.
The cached-hit branch (forceRefresh=false with a young snapshot) does NOT call saveSecuritySnapshot.
No new scan is triggered by the change; ResourceSecurityAggregationService is unchanged and still cannot trigger a scan.
`mvn -q -pl xamops-service -am test -Dtest=SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest` passes, and ResourceSecurityControllerTest + CurInsightsControllerTest stay green.
findings: Implemented in SecurityController.getSecurityFindings: inside the existing live-scan .thenApply(findings -> ...) branch, after `merged = resolutions.reconcileAgainstFreshScan(...)` and before `return ResponseEntity.ok(merged)`, added `dashboardDataService.saveSecuritySnapshot(cacheKey, merged);` reusing the already-declared `cacheKey = "security-" + accountId`. No new scan trigger added; the cached (forceRefresh=false hit) branch and ResourceSecurityAggregationService are untouched — the aggregator still cannot trigger a scan. New test SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest (2 tests) mocks all 9 controller deps via MockitoExtension: positive case calls getSecurityFindings(AWS_ID,true), stubs mergeInto/reconcileAgainstFreshScan as pass-through, and verifies saveSecuritySnapshot(eq("security-"+AWS_ID), any()); negative case calls getSecurityFindings(AWS_ID,false) with a young cached snapshot and verifies saveSecuritySnapshot is never called. Verification: `mvn -q -pl xamops-service compile` BUILD SUCCESS; `mvn -q -pl xamops-service -am test -Dtest=SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest,ResourceSecurityControllerTest,CurInsightsControllerTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` -> SnapshotPersist 2/2, ResourceSecurityController 6/6, CurInsightsController 36/36, all 0 failures/errors. Note for convergence: the `-am` flag pulls in dependency modules (e.g. permissions-common) that have no matching tests, so the targeted test run requires -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false to avoid a spurious no-tests-executed failure in those modules.
